about: The Last Call's first piece of work, 'Tabs close at dawn' (for-review/design/characters-and-vendor-quests.md, Part C, 1, Part 1). Three regulars have let one night's tab run a week, and Captain Dolores will not write it down. Marks: d1 (2 taken, 100 done), tab.w, tab.g, tab.c (the Warden corporal's twelve, the winch hand's nine, the collector's thirteen: 1 got out of them, 2 sold to the book), d1.how (1 collected, 3 paid out of the player's own water), d1.sold (the three names sold to Mother Ledger), dolores (what she thinks: -1 an enemy). CALLS THAT ARE MINE: 'win it at her tables' is not here, since neither of her games is built; the winch hand can be met half way.
name: Tabs close at dawn
giver: Captain Dolores, on the Apron of the Last Call
steps: Three regulars at the Last Call owe a week-old tab: a Warden corporal 12 L, a winch hand 9 L, a Chainmen collector 13 L. They are on the Apron. Bring Captain Dolores the 34 L, however it is come by.
The tabs at the Last Call are settled, one way or another.

Captain Dolores.words: I have a job for you, sweetheart. Three of my regulars have not paid for what they drank. The Warden corporal owes me twelve litres. The winch hand owes nine. The Chainmen's collector owes thirteen. All three are out here on the Apron tonight. Get it out of them, thirty-four litres in all, and bring it to my table. Eight of it is yours, and you get the better jobs off my board.

answers.log: Took Captain Dolores's work: three tabs at the Last Call, 34 L in all.

Captain Dolores.words: The corporal is down at the south tables. The collector is by the fire. The winch hand is at the north end, by the tail. Ask them, lean on them, pay it yourself: how is your business. One rule. I keep no book, and none of this goes to Mother Ledger. Sell her their names and you and I are finished.
You have not brought me my thirty-four yet, sweetheart. Get it from the three of them, or put it down yourself.

answers.words: I will cover it myself. (34 L)
answers.log: Paid three strangers' tabs at the Last Call out of my own water.

Captain Dolores.words: All three. Then count it onto my table, and we are square before the sign goes off.

answers.log: Brought Captain Dolores the three tabs: 34 L. She paid 8.

Captain Dolores.words: That is the bar square. Eight for you. And the board has better cards on it for people I can count on.
You paid for three people you do not know. I will know by morning whether that makes you kind or a fool, and either way you drink here. Eight back, and the good cards.
You sold my regulars to the book. Three people with pages, out of my bar, and my bar had none. The exits are here, and here. Use one.
Captain Dolores.log: Captain Dolores knows who sold her regulars' tabs to Mother Ledger.

Captain Dolores.words: Seat-belt sign is on for you, sweetheart. Sit down somewhere else.
Seat-belt sign is off. Sit anywhere. If you hear anything worth a drink, you know which table is mine.

A Warden corporal.words: Twelve? The Captain can whistle for it. I am Wardens. We drink where we like and the bar is glad of it.

answers.words: She stops pouring for the post until it is paid. Her words.

A Warden corporal.words: All right. All right! Here. Twelve. You have a face I will know again.
She would, too. Twelve. Tell her it was a slow week on the wall.
It is paid. Go and lean on somebody else.
I have a page. Twelve litres, and now I have a page in her book. Do you know what the Captain does to a Warden with a page? Neither do I. Yet.

A winch hand.words: Nine. I know it is nine. The Skip has been down four days, and nine is what I have in the world.

answers.words: Give me five. I will find the other four.

A winch hand.words: Take it. That was the week's bread.
You would... yes. Five. I will not forget who stood four litres for a winch hand.
Paid. The cable moves tomorrow, they say. They said that yesterday.
Nine litres. For nine litres I am in the book. My mother was in the book.

A Chainmen collector.words: Thirteen. I collect. I am not collected from. Ask Harrow how that goes.

answers.words: Thirteen, or the Captain says your name at the bar with the other two.

A Chainmen collector.words: Thirteen. Harrow will hear who leans on a collector over a bar tab.
You have had your thirteen. Do not stand there.
She bought my tab. Mother Ledger bought a collector's bar tab. I write pages. I do not have one. Somebody is laughing, and it is not me.

doors.said: A new card, in a careful hand: TWENTY LITRES for the reader who brought ILYA BRANDT to the gate. M. Brandt. Somebody has torn the corner off it already.

The good cards are out. A hauler wants a second pair of eyes on the salt road. Hide & Plate wants road signs, any. Brass wants somebody who does not ask what is in the crate. None of them can be taken up yet.
Cards, tucked in rows. Somebody has lost a dog and will pay for the collar back. Somebody wants a wall watched. The Captain keeps the good cards for people she can count on.

Mother Ledger.words: Three tabs at the Last Call. I have wanted a page out of that bar for eleven years. Seventeen litres, for the three names.

answers.words: Sell her the three names. (17 L)
answers.does: d1.sold=1 water+17 st.chainmen+5 tab.w=2 tab.g=2 tab.c=2
answers.log: Sold three bar tabs from the Last Call to Mother Ledger for 17 L. Three people have pages.

Mother Ledger.words: Written down. Each of them has a page by morning. She will know before she next restocks. They always know.
